# snappy / snappy_compress_fuzzer

snappy's own fuzz target `snappy_compress_fuzzer` ([source](source/snappy_compress_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over snappy 1.3.1 (google/snappy at 9c28114a).

Checks 5 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: For every compression level MinCompressionLevel()..MaxCompressionLevel(): Uncompress(Compress(input, level)) == input, full std::string equality.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against snappy 1.3.1 at commit 9c28114a.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The size returned by Compress equals the size of the output string it wrote ([lines 45-50](source/snappy_compress_fuzzer.cc#L45-L50)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Compressed length never exceeds the documented worst-case bound MaxCompressedLength(input.size()) ([line 51](source/snappy_compress_fuzzer.cc#L51)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- The just-produced compressed buffer is accepted by the validator IsValidCompressedBuffer ([lines 52-53](source/snappy_compress_fuzzer.cc#L52-L53)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- For every compression level MinCompressionLevel()..MaxCompressionLevel(): Uncompress(Compress(input, level)) == input, full std::string equality ([lines 55-61](source/snappy_compress_fuzzer.cc#L55-L61)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Uncompress of a buffer produced by Compress reports success ([line 60](source/snappy_compress_fuzzer.cc#L60)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.

A failure of any of the checks at lines 45-50, line 51, lines 52-53 and lines 55-61 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name them exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies them on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other check.

Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch snappy` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
